memos.scout:
The honest case for buying FIAT now is weak, and I don't think the brief supports a buy.

The strongest points: it's alive, has broad participation (754 curve buyers, 429 buyers in the first two minutes ex-agent, top-5 buyer share only 13.5%, top-3 curve share 5.4%), and the last 15 minutes show net positive flow (+10.7 SOL) with a +24.9% return. Those are real signs of organic interest, and the class label is ORGANIC.

But the demand isn't holding. The coin is down 56% from its 30-minute high and -37.6% over 30 minutes. In the last 15 minutes, sell SOL (139.2) nearly matched buy SOL (149.9), with a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.96 in the early window, and 280 sellers versus 309 buyers. Half the curve was bundled (50.6%), which points to coordinated early buying. The 15-minute gain is a bounce inside a larger decline, and a bounce like that is exactly what has lost money on average. With a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost on a 67.7 SOL pool, I'd need a sustained move to clear fees, and nothing here shows one.

Verdict: no buy. The organic label and recent net inflow are real, but they don't outweigh a deep drawdown, heavy bundling, and sell pressure that hasn't cleared.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss here is a dump by the bundle holders. Bundle share is 50.6% of the curve, and the completer holds 39.6%, so roughly half the supply sits with coordinated wallets that can exit into any bid. The last 15 minutes show sell SOL of 139.2 against buy SOL of 149.9, with net flow only +10.7 SOL and sellers (280) nearly matching buyers (309). That is distribution pressure, not accumulation. The 30-minute high has already been drawn down 56%, and the sell-to-buy ratio of 0.96 in the first two minutes after graduation shows the launch was mostly sold into. With a 67.7 SOL pool, a $20 ticket faces a 1.4-5.1% round trip before any move, and a 25% bounce would need to beat that plus the bundle overhang. Skip.
